candidate.educational_objective: Provide nonstigmatizing, individualized acute-pain assessment and advocacy for a client with opioid use disorder.

options.A: Agree to withhold analgesia until objective signs of pain appear, because a substance use history makes the client's self-report too unreliable for treatment decisions.
options.B: Reassess the pain and clinical status, use nonstigmatizing communication, and advocate for an individualized analgesia plan that addresses both pain and safety needs.
options.C: Tell the client that pain medication will be reconsidered only after the substance use disorder is fully treated, because addiction care takes priority over acute pain.
options.D: Avoid discussing the comment with the team and give only nonpharmacologic measures, because challenging a colleague could interfere with the treatment relationship.

candidate.rationale: A history of opioid use disorder does not eliminate the need for appropriate acute-pain assessment and management. CDC guidance emphasizes ongoing pain management for patients with substance use disorder and recommends nonjudgmental communication because stigma can interfere with care. The nurse should reassess pain and clinical status and advocate for an individualized plan that addresses analgesia and safety rather than dismissing the report as “drug-seeking.”
candidate.source_claim_supported: Patients with opioid use disorder still require appropriate acute-pain assessment and management; nonjudgmental communication and individualized care reduce stigma-related barriers.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain — United States, 2022
candidate.source_locator: Recommendation 12 implementation / Pain Management for Patients with Opioid Use Disorder — co-occurring pain and OUD require ongoing pain management; use nonjudgmental communication and avoid stigma
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A client with a history of opioid use disorder reports severe postoperative pain. A team member says, 'They are probably drug-seeking, so we should avoid treating the pain.' Which nursing response is best?
